clue.text: Desire a piano, small and dainty

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
petite describes someone small and neatly built

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a little piano, compact and delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving or longing, the same as a desire.

clue.text: It's a separate state, unfortunately

annotationWithheld.why: It's a separate state, unfortunately (4): ALAS is defined by 'unfortunately', but no parse of 'It's a separate state' gives the letters without stretching (ALASKA less KA has no indicator); no source found

clue.text: Knock and slightly wound

explanation.surface: Someone gives a light blow and leaves a minor injury.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine knocks or pinks when fuel ignites early; in fencing, to pink is to nick an opponent lightly.

clue.text: Doll found in the Easter collection

indicators.note: a collection gathers these letters together in a new grouping, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toy doll turns up among the Easter gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is the prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2. 'collection' signals that the letters of THE EASTER are gathered into a new order; 'found in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll is the first name of Shakespeare's Tearsheet, so the forename stands for the character's surname.

clue.text: Workers' joint units producing something wonderful

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers, so 'workers'' is read as belonging to the bees
knees are joints, counted here as units of the body

explanation.surface: Employees' shared bits of equipment turn out to be marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint units' looks like shared equipment, but it means body joints, the knees of the worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something excellent or first-rate is the bee's knees.

clue.text: A way into mine over the hill

indicators.note: the phrase going into the mine places the first pieces inside the pit

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A path leads into a mine on the far side of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the hill' reads as geography but is the definition: too old.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too old to do the job is described idiomatically as past their best.

clue.text: In Asian city, you'll find old marketplace

indicators.note: the word In at the front says the next piece is placed inside the Asian city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Visit an Indian city and you will come upon an ancient market.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square and market in an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Magic trio moved around clubs, arousing mixed emotions

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit around the card suit letter
the letters of magic trio are moved into a different order

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Three magicians tour the nightclubs, getting laughs and tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' scrambles the two fodder words into TRAGIOMIC; 'around' wraps that round the clubs letter. The surface trio of magicians is pure decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something both tragic and comic stirs sadness and laughter together.

clue.text: Jeremiah, for one, confused Ted, in short

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bewildered Ted, put briefly, is compared to the prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly', but all three words are the anagram fodder for 'confused'. Jeremiah is traditionally the author of Lamentations.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer or writer of laments is one; Jeremiah wrote the Book of Lamentations.

clue.text: Toughened girl got better after ditching husband

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the husband's letter is removed

parts.note: healed means recovered from illness

explanation.surface: A hardened woman recovered once she was rid of her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toughened' looks like describing the girl, but is the definition: metal annealed by heating and cooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats then slowly cools metal or glass to make it stronger and less brittle.

clue.text: Empty words in latest song

parts.note: hot means newest, as in hot off the press
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A new hit single has meaningless lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk with no substance is idiomatically called a lot of hot air.

clue.text: People selfish today — conclusion of my parents' meeting

explanation.surface: The self-centred young are what came of a couple getting together.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads cryptically: what my parents' meeting concluded in was the making of me.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1970s were dubbed the self-absorbed decade; the second sense is producing me by procreation.

clue.text: Like a few short of money, shifted into profession

parts.note: as means like, in the way of

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the money letter is taken out

parts.note: several means a few
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lacking cash, a handful moved into a new line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profession' looks like a career but means declaring. 'shifted' turns INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess is to declare openly, so a profession is a solemn affirmation.

clue.text: Frank married off friends to eligible people

parts.note: candid means frank and open

indicators.note: off means removed, so the married letter goes

parts.note: mates are friends

explanation.surface: Frank married and then left his friends for suitable partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are people eligible or standing for selection.

clue.text: Seeing American teenager, policeman soundly beats her

parts.note: bobby is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: soundly here means said aloud, not thoroughly

parts.note: beats means socks, and her is dropped to 'er in speech

explanation.surface: A police officer, seeing a US teenager, gives her a good thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals that SOCKS 'ER is heard as SOXER. A bobby-soxer was a 1940s American teenage girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby-soxers were 1940s American teenage girls, named for their ankle socks.

clue.text: Conductor describing Purcell's work for St Cecilia's Day

definitions.text: Purcell's work for St Cecilia's Day

explanation.surface: A conductor talks about a Purcell piece for the music saint's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra, but means an electrode. Purcell wrote an ode for St Cecilia's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode that conducts current; the second sense is a celebratory poem set to music.

clue.text: Offensive weapon permit held — what an obscenity

indicators.note: held means contained, so the permit word sits inside the weapon

parts.note: a sword is a weapon for attack
wear means allow, as in he won't wear it

explanation.surface: A licence for an attack weapon is being held: disgraceful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'what an obscenity' is the definition: the expletive itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscenity is a curse or profane expletive.

clue.text: Central part in Verdi I perform, allowed to take title role

indicators.note: the central part of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: go means work or function, as in the engine will go
let means allowed

explanation.surface: In a Verdi opera, I sing the lead, given leave to play the title part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central part in Verdi' looks like the opera's lead but gives R, the middle of VERDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is the hunchback jester who names Verdi's opera.

clue.text: Money owed round university, a gambling sum — one was brought to court

indicators.note: the debt goes round the university letter

parts.note: a debt is money owed
an ante is a stake put in before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A debt from university and a gambling stake end up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to court' suggests a law court, but means presented at the royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman making her first formal entry into society was presented at court.

clue.text: Boasting about home wins

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boasting word goes round home

parts.note: gas is empty boastful talk
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone brags about winning at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains are winnings or profits.

clue.text: It's rude to stop working without consent

indicators.note: without means outside, so the stop word wraps round consent

parts.note: to disable a machine is to stop it working
agree means consent

explanation.surface: Downing tools without permission is impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-mannered or unpleasant is disagreeable, a near synonym of rude.

clue.text: Information about a type of painting

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Notes about a style of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Genre is a category of art, and genre painting depicts everyday scenes.

clue.text: Green half of Irish town

indicators.note: only half of the town name is kept, the rest removed

parts.note: Limerick is a city in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: The colour green covers half of an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime is a bright yellowish-green colour.

clue.text: Parking in Paris is a nuisance

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space in Paris is a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing.

clue.text: After a short time, firing be comes stressful

indicators.note: After places the firing word behind the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
axing means sacking, firing

explanation.surface: After a brief interval, a sacking becomes a strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'becomes' at a line break; 'becomes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxing means demanding or burdensome.

clue.text: Strong criticism of ethnic group after assistance is rejected

indicators.note: after puts the ethnic group behind the assistance piece
rejected means sent back, so the assistance word is read backwards

parts.note: aid is assistance
a tribe is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: An ethnic group is attacked once its offer of help is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, forceful verbal attack.

clue.text: Show hide to vet

explanation.surface: An exhibition conceals a visit to the animal doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'vet' is a verb, not the animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to show a film, to conceal behind a barrier, and to check someone thoroughly.

clue.text: Advanced in party initially, without much energy

indicators.note: initially says the phrase in party goes at the front, before the advanced piece

parts.note: a do is a party
lent means advanced, as of money

explanation.surface: Getting ahead at a party early on, then flagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but here it means 'at the start': the phrase 'in party' comes before 'Advanced'.
explanation.definitionFit: An indolent person is lazy and inactive.
